claims.text: Setting the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service lets Terraform and OpenTofu use the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud as a state backend.
The page links to the Terraform state backend guide at /docs/integrations/terraform/state-backend/, which must exist.
PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is an environment variable on the self-hosted Pulumi Cloud API service that specifies the domain serving the Terraform-compatible API (e.g. `tf.pulumiapi.acmecorp.com`).
When PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN is unset in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the Terraform-compatible API is disabled and its routes are not registered.
The DNS record for the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN domain should point at the same host that serves PULUMI_API_DOMAIN in self-hosted Pulumi Cloud.
In self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN may be set to the same value as PULUMI_API_DOMAIN; a separate domain is not required.
The Terraform state backend guide uses `tf.pulumi.com` as the domain in the Terraform/OpenTofu configuration, the `terraform login`/`tofu login` command, and the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.

For self-hosted Pulumi Cloud, the PULUMI_TFE_DOMAIN value replaces `tf.pulumi.com` in the Terraform or OpenTofu configuration, in `terraform login` / `tofu login`, and in the `TF_TOKEN_*` variable name.
